title: VOICE FOR THE VOICELESS: ACTIVE SAMPLING TO DETECT COMMENTS SUPPORTING THE ROHINGYAS
findings: The online discourse surrounding the Rohingya crisis contains a significant religion-centric dimension. Topic modeling of user comments revealed three main themes: a geopolitical discussion, a religion-centric discussion with an appeal for help, and a distinct 'anti-Islamic cluster' primarily consisting of religion-themed slurs. This indicates that religion is a central and polarizing element in the public discussion of the crisis.

measurement_description: Detection of supportive speech ('help-speech') for the Rohingya minority within a broader online discourse characterized by religious conflict. The analysis also involved identifying and characterizing religion-centric discussions and anti-Islamic slurs.
